Subject: Trial staging & capacity proposal — next steps and POC schedule

Thanks again for the productive call this morning — appreciated the clarity on success metrics. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we lock the POC schedule.

Summary of agreed success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for 1k token prompt mix (weighted).
- Throughput: sustain 30 requests/sec for steady-state evaluation, peaks up to 150 req/s for burst scenarios.
- Quality: top-1 pass rate on the provided evaluation set >= 92% (per your labeled test corpus).
- Security/Data: model inputs stay in your VPC; no model telemetry leaves the tenant boundary.

POC evaluation plan (high-level):
- Week 0 (Nov 16–18): environment staging + model pin (baseline model weights) + smoke tests.
- Week 1 (Nov 19–23): baseline runs (latency/throughput, correctness on eval set).
- Week 2 (Nov 24–28): load tests, autoscaler tuning, burst simulations; analyze cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Week 3 (Dec 1–4): final acceptance runs and handover checklist.

Ownership (confirmed):
- Nimbus: Alex (product owner), Nikki (eng lead).
- Redwood: Priyom (sales lead, MPA/signature coordination), Ben Carter (solutions owner — runtime/config), Lauren Bishop (infra ops — GPU scheduling & autoscaler).

Capacity proposal (initial ask):
- Reserve 2 x A100-80GB (baseline) for Nov 16–30 to ensure stable perf during initial baseline runs.
- Autoscaling policy: start at 2 GPUs; scale up at 65% sustained GPU utilization to 8 GPUs for sustained load. Allow short-duration burst up to 12 GPUs (pre-warmed) for traffic spikes (<= 10 minutes).
- Warm/cold effects: plan for a short warm-up penalty on first large seqs — we recommend pre-warming cache during staging windows.

Cost/terms: we will provide a reserved-rate estimate for the 2-GPU baseline and separate on-demand/burst pricing for additional capacity. If you want a firm number, we can attach a short cost appendix — Ben will put that together.

Attachments: Redwood_POC_SOW.pdf (stub), POC_resourcing.xlsx (stub).

Next actions (requesting confirmation by COB Wed Nov 11):
1) Confirm success criteria above or propose edits.
2) Confirm you want the baseline reservation Nov 16–30.
3) Confirm primary eval dataset and deliver to us (S3 link or share in call notes).

I’ll schedule a 30-min sync with Ben and Lauren for Thursday to review the autoscaler knobs and labeling ingestion.

Thanks,
Priyom

Thanks, Priyom — that lines up with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Autoscaling fallback: If the autoscaler can't reach additional GPUs (capacity constrained), what is the fallback behavior? We want to ensure we don't see silent failures — prefer graceful degraded mode (limit concurrency + queue).

2) Week 2 burst testing: we plan to run three 15-minute blast windows at 10x normal traffic. Will pre-warming the KV cache plus having pre-provisioned burst capacity be sufficient, or do we need an extended warm window?

3) Cost ask: please include an estimate for (a) reserved 2-GPU baseline for 2 weeks, (b) sustained scale to 8 GPUs for a 4-hour prove-out, and (c) two 15-minute bursts to 12 GPUs. We need a line item to circulate to finance.

4) Scheduling constraint: our team prefers business-hours-only for the reserved baseline (Mon–Fri, 8:00–18:00 PT). Can Redwood restrict the reservation to those windows?

If those are feasible we'll sign the MPA. Nikki and I will confirm dataset delivery timeline after Ben shares the ingestion steps.

— Alex

Subject: Re: Trial staging & capacity proposal — sizing and autoscaler knobs

Priyom / Lauren — quick technical proposal to answer Alex's questions and give a concrete config that we can include in the SOW: 

Concrete capacity plan (recommendation):
- Baseline reservation: 2 x A100-80GB (Mon–Fri, 08:00–18:00 PT) from Nov 16–30 as requested.
- Autoscaler policy: min_replicas=2, scale_up_trigger=GPU_util >= 65% for 2 consecutive windows (1 minute windows), scale_step=+2 nodes, max_replicas=8 for sustained scale.
- Burst window: short-burst override to max_burst_replicas=12 with pre-warm flag — these are short-lived (<= 15 minutes) and require on-demand capacity; pre-warm should be triggered 5 minutes before the scheduled blast.
- Fallback behavior: graceful degrade = queueing + concurrency limit per worker (configurable); when scale cannot provision, requests receive 429 with Retry-After header and a degraded-mode header so callers can surface it.

Operational notes:
- Cold-start: model KV cache warm-up expected to add ~5–10% to p95 during the first 3–5 minutes after scale event. Pre-warm reduces this to ~1–2%.
- Canary: recommend canary rollout for each model variant in the production cluster (10% traffic) for 24 hours prior to full evaluation.
- Logging & metrics: we will expose token-level latency, GPU utilization, batch sizes, and queue depth into the Redwood Console for live monitoring.

Costing (estimates; final will be added to SOW):
- Reserved 2-GPU baseline (2 weeks, business-hours-only): see POC_resourcing.xlsx — ballpark $X,XXX (reserved discount applied).
- Sustained scale to 8 GPUs for a 4-hour prove-out: $Y,YYY on top of baseline.
- Two 15-minute bursts to 12 GPUs: $ZZZ (on-demand).

I'll tidy the numbers and add them to the SOW appendix. If they want strict cost caps we can set a spend guardrail in the autoscaler.

Ben
